real_conflicts: The proposal to 'increase the scale and weight of the secondary text' (Composition Verdict) threatens the visual hierarchy and atmospheric depth. The current low-contrast, smaller text allows the background to recede, creating a sense of vast, dark space. Enlarging this text would clutter the bottom third, competing with the 'spark' visual and destroying the moody, urgent atmosphere required by the brief.

The proposal to 'shift the headline to the upper-left quadrant' (Composition Verdict) disrupts the color balance. The current central placement anchors the white text against the darkest part of the gradient. Moving it would likely place it over the lighter, abstract background shapes, reducing legibility and breaking the stark contrast that defines the poster's visual impact.
accepted: The proposal to 'replace the abstract background with a deep, atmospheric silhouette of a mountain ridge' (Visual Concept Verdict) is essential. The current background is too sterile and fails to ground the concept of 'wild' in a physical landscape. A silhouette provides the necessary tonal contrast for the fire line to pop against.

The proposal to 'apply a gradient fill... transitioning from dark earth tones at the bottom to glowing orange/yellow' (Visual Concept Verdict) aligns with my mandate. The current flat, neon glow is gratuitous; a gradient that fades into smoke or darkness will integrate the fire line into the environment, creating a cohesive color system.
concession: I concede that the current 'spark' icon is too generic and vector-like. It lacks the textural grit of a real ember. I agree that the visual metaphor needs to be more organic to support the 'wild' theme.
compromise: We will replace the abstract background with a dark, textured mountain silhouette (Visual Concept) to ground the composition. However, we will keep the headline centered (rejecting the Composition shift) to maintain the high-contrast focal point. The 'fire line' will be transformed into a textured flame front that interacts with the mountain silhouette, using the gradient colors proposed, but we will keep the secondary text small and subtle to preserve the atmospheric depth.
nonnegotiable: The headline 'ONE SPARK IS ENOUGH' must remain the primary focal point with high-contrast white typography. Any changes to the background or imagery must serve to enhance, not distract from, this text.
